plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack with gradient-thickness optimization can achieve dual-band spectral separation (high reflectance 300-450 nm, high transmittance 1000-1700 nm) on fused silica. The route draws from recalled thin-film design practice: quarter-wave stacks create stopbands, and non-quarter-wave thickness tuning can broaden or shift bands. This iteration repairs the previous compilation failure by using the gradient_thickness optimizer that succeeded in iterations 04, 08, and 12, and adjusts the thickness perturbation bounds to ensure feasible candidates pass validation.

routes.title: 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic with gradient thickness optimization and relaxed perturbation bounds
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with individually tunable layer thicknesses can simultaneously achieve high reflectance in 300-450 nm and high transmittance in 1000-1700 nm at normal incidence on fused silica, with the gradient-thickness optimizer finding a non-quarter-wave solution that balances both bands.
routes.design_principle: Recalled thin-film physics: dielectric mirrors use alternating high/low index layers to create photonic stopbands via constructive interference of reflections. Quarter-wave thicknesses (λ/4n) center stopbands at design wavelengths, but deviating from quarter-wave can broaden bands or create multiple passbands. HfO2 (high index ~2.0-2.1 in SWIR) and SiO2 (low index ~1.45) provide sufficient index contrast for reflectance in UV/blue while remaining transparent in SWIR.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 coating layers total, alternating starting with HfO2 at air interface)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers
thickness perturbation bounds ±18 nm for initial feasibility search
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
maintain physical validity (no negative thicknesses, no material property violations)
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 24 (within 30-layer limit)
all thicknesses must be positive and within depositor capability (20-200 nm range)
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard evaporatable/sputterable dielectrics
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks produce stopbands centered at design wavelength; deviating from quarter-wave shifts and broadens stopbands.
Recalled: Index contrast between HfO2 and SiO2 is sufficient for high reflectance with ~12-15 layer pairs in UV/blue.
Recalled: Both HfO2 and SiO2 have low extinction coefficients in 1000-1700 nm, enabling high transmittance.
Recalled: Gradient-based thickness optimization can find local optima in multilayer design spaces when initialized near quarter-wave values.
Recalled: Normal incidence simplifies design as polarization splitting is not a factor.
expected_advantages: 24 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization without exceeding manufacturing limits
Alternating high/low index pattern is a known working topology for dichroics
Gradient optimizer successfully produced target scores above 0.81 in prior iterations 04 and 12
Relaxed perturbation bounds (±18 nm vs ±12 nm) should increase feasible candidate yield
known_risks: Uncertain whether 24 layers is optimal vs 20 or 28 layers - this route does not explore layer count as a variable, so the true optimum pair count is unknown.
Uncertain exact refractive index values of hfo2 and sio2 datasets in the registry at 300 nm and 1700 nm endpoints - these are measured data, not design variables, but affect achievable performance.
Uncertain whether gradient optimizer will converge to global vs local optimum - multiple starting points would be needed to verify, but this route uses single initialization.
The ±18 nm perturbation bound is a hypothesis based on feedback directive; if it still produces zero valid candidates, the bound may need further relaxation or a different optimizer method.
No angle or polarization specified in original request - assumed normal incidence and unpolarized or average polarization; if actual use requires oblique angles, performance may degrade.
routes.execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence at normal angle (0 degrees). Use exactly 24 layers in alternating sequence: HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand) (HfO2 first at air interface, SiO2 (Lemarchand) last at substrate). Optimize all 24 layer thicknesses individually within bounds 20-200 nm using gradient_thickness optimizer with perturbation bounds ±18 nm. Maximize dual-band objective: mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band with equal weighting. Use coherent transfer-matrix method. Total layer count is fixed at 24. Materials are hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from the guaranteed registry.
routes.revision_reason: Repair compilation failure from iteration 15 (unsupported optimizer method) by reverting to gradient_thickness optimizer that succeeded in iterations 04, 08, 12. Implement feedback directive to relax thickness perturbation bounds from ±12 nm to ±18 nm to increase feasible candidate yield. Maintain 24-layer topology and material sequence from prior successful iterations.

unresolved_decisions: Whether 24 layers is the optimal count vs 20, 22, 26, or 28 layers - this route does not vary layer count, so the true optimum is unknown without running additional axes.
Whether starting with HfO2 at air interface is optimal vs starting with SiO2 - this route fixes the order and does not explore the reverse sequence.

The exact refractive index dispersion of hfo2 and sio2 in the registry at band edges (300 nm, 1700 nm) - these are measured properties, not design variables, but they determine achievable performance limits.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route fails to produce any physically valid candidates after three rounds with relaxed perturbation bounds, the problem may require a different topology (e.g., chirped stack, defect cavity, or different material pair) that this control axis does not explore. Stop and flag for architectural revision.

if valid_candidates equals 0 for two consecutive rounds despite ±18 nm perturbation bounds, stop and flag for topology revision (layer count or material order change)
if tightest_margin falls below 0.0 for more than 50 percent of candidates in a round, reduce perturbation bounds to ±10 nm and continue

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
